chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Hammad from Hariz from al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
My grandfather, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), would give his fitrah to the weak, and to the one who has no one, and to the one who has no guardian.

And his father (Imam al-Hassan) (peace be upon him) said: It belongs to its owners, unless they are not found; if they are not found, then to the one who is not set up (i.e., not appointed as a recipient).
And it is not transferred from one land to another.
And the Imam places it wherever he wishes and does in it what he sees fit.

key_terms.أَهْلِهَا: Its owners: The primary designated recipients of the fitrah.
key_terms.الإِمَام: The Imam: The divinely appointed leader who has authority over the distribution of fitrah.
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللّهِ: The Messenger of Allah: Referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
key_terms.فِطْرَة: Fitrah: A specific charity or stipend distributed by the Imam or Prophet, often associated with specific recipients.
key_terms.يَنصِبُ: Set up/Appointed: Referring to being designated or established as a recipient or guardian.

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to receive the fitrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the hierarchy of fitrah recipients, prioritizing the weak and those without guardians, while establishing that the Imam holds discretionary authority (tasarruf) over its distribution within the local region. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that fitrah is not strictly bound to the six categories of Zakat but is tied to the concept of Wilayah and local need, allowing the Imam to allocate it where he sees fit if the primary owners are unavailable.
